_comment: Provenance catalog loaded by the publisher (RF-08, RD-01, RD-05). Values come from RAP-LM-DATA source_manifest.json (capture 2026-11-17) and the fused dataset report. Licence text is what could be verified; 'to verify' marks terms not stated in the captured file.

target_definition.population: All pedestrian collisions (any severity and subtype)
target_definition.definition: Every recorded collision with a pedestrian involved: run over, hit-and-run, collision followed by run over, or any crash with a pedestrian victim, regardless of injury severity. Latent intensity estimated on the police-census reporting scale.
target_definition.value_unit: expected recorded pedestrian collisions per km2 per year (annualised for the day type and 6-hour band)
target_definition.index_method: risk_index = percentile rank (0-100) of the indicator in the frozen reference distribution of training-year estimates of the same spatial view.

sources.name: Censo Nacional de Comisarias (CENACOM) 2012-2017, traffic accident and person modules (DBF microdata)
sources.licence: Public statistical microdata (INEI); attribution. Reuse terms to verify.
sources.spatial_coverage: 43 districts; 2011-2014 by reporting police-station district, 2015-2017 by occurrence district; points derived only by street matching
sources.population: All severities reported to police stations

sources.name: BBDD ONSV siniestros fatales 2021-2025 (preliminar) with persons table
sources.licence: Public download from ONSV; attribution. Reuse terms to verify.
sources.spatial_coverage: 43 districts, georeferenced points (validated inside the declared district)
sources.population: Crashes with at least one fatal victim and a pedestrian involved (severity-truncated observation of the target)

sources.name: Limites distritales, provincia de Lima (43 districts, UBIGEO 1501xx)
sources.spatial_coverage: 43 districts of the province of Lima; Callao excluded

sources.name: Lima.osm.pbf city extract
sources.spatial_coverage: Lima extract clipped to the 43 districts
sources.population: Named streets (2026 network) used for street length and police-reference geocoding

sources.name: Transit stops, public transport routes, traffic lights, pedestrian crossings, road types (layers 303, 304, 309, 314, 315)
sources.licence: Public ArcGIS REST service; attribution. Reuse terms to verify.
sources.spatial_coverage: Lima; partial coverage in some districts (absence of a feature is not proof of absence)

sources.publisher: Municipalidad de San Isidro (Plataforma Nacional de Datos Abiertos)
sources.name: Apoyo en accidentes de transito 2026
sources.exclusion_reason: One municipality, partial year 2026 and no event time: cannot be assigned to a time band nor compared across the 43 districts.

sources.name: Accidents by department 2015-2025, by type 2020-2025; INEI security statistics 2025
sources.exclusion_reason: Aggregated by department or type without district, date or location: usable only as magnitude checks, not as events.

sources.name: Accidents on national and concession roads
sources.spatial_coverage: National highways and concessions, not the urban network
sources.exclusion_reason: Highway network outside the urban street population of the 43 districts; no individual georeference for most records.

variables.label: Pedestrian collisions located to cell (point, intersection or street)
variables.description: Previous-year events by cell; CENACOM and ONSV kept as separate channels.

variables.label: Pedestrian collisions by district
variables.description: Previous-year district density including events not located to a cell.

variables.label: Fatal pedestrian crashes (ONSV)
variables.description: Severity-truncated observation linked to the latent intensity by a learned reporting factor.

variables.label: Injury severity grade per collision
variables.description: Not used as model input: grades are incomplete and change between editions. Shown only as historical record (injured, deceased).

variables.label: Resident population
variables.description: Sum of 100 m WorldPop cells inside each 1 km cell (log, standardised).

variables.label: Measured pedestrian volume
variables.description: No public pedestrian count covering the 43 districts was found; exposure is represented only by proxies.

variables.label: Vehicle traffic volume
variables.description: Toll counts exist only for concession highways; no urban traffic volume for the 43 districts.

limitations.description: No source observes July 2017 to December 2020; those years are not published. CENACOM 2017 covers January-June only (handled as a coverage offset).

2021-2024 are observed only through fatal crashes (ONSV). The model links them to the all-severity intensity with one city-wide reporting factor; local differences in fatality share are not identified.

CENACOM has no coordinates. Events are placed by matching police road references with OSM streets in the declared district: intersections as points, single streets spread along their length, unmatched events only at district level. Block numbers are not converted.
2011-2014 CENACOM records carry the police-station district, not the occurrence district (6-7 % mismatch measured where both exist).
Context layers are 2020-2026 snapshots used for every year; historical infrastructure changes are not represented.
No measured pedestrian exposure. Population, stops and routes are proxies; the indicator is not a probability nor a rate per pedestrian.
Police records under-report collisions without complaint; the indicator is on the recorded scale and is relative.
Analytical reference for specialists. It does not prescribe interventions and is not a real-time prediction (RG-02, RG-03).
